title: Characterization of CdTe Back-Contacts with Thick Alumina Reflectors
content: CdTe-based photovoltaic (PV) technology offers a viable and sustainable solution to satisfy the growing energy demand. One of the key approaches to enhancing cell efficiency is to implement a passivated and selective back contact [1]. Among various candidate materials, Al2O3 has shown excellent passivation due to its fixed negative charge and chemical modification at the CdTe/Al2O3 interface [2]. Previous studies have demonstrated that a thin Al2O3 (a few nanometers to tens of nanometers) can improve solar cell performance [3, 4]. However, the inherent surface roughness of the CdTe absorber layer may lead to non-uniform passivation, potentially limiting performance gains. In this work, we investigate the use of a thicker Al2O3 on CdTe solar cells with roughness comparable to CdTe absorber layer. Point-contact geometry is used in the Al2O3 reflector layer to promote the majority carrier collection, while reflecting minority carriers. The structural and compositional properties of the patterned back-contacts are characterized using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS).
